context: Policy enforcement state where traffic is logged but not blocked. UI actions: 'Save as Simulation'. Enum: MONITOR_ONLY.

cli_recipes.intent: Count policies currently in Simulation (monitor-only) mode for the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Single GraphQL call — returns {dateTime, monitorMode, value}. Use --site to scope to one or more sites.

cli_recipes.intent: List traffic that hit policies in Simulation mode over the last 24h
cli_recipes.notes: PolicyStatus=SIMULATION corresponds to policies in MONITOR_ONLY enforcement.

cli_recipes.intent: Filter the full policy stream to only Simulation policies
cli_recipes.notes: JMESPath filter over the per-policy ndjson stream. The per-policy enforcement field is monitorMode (not enforcementState); get-all-as-nd-json returns policy SETS, not policies.

context: Policy enforcement state where traffic is actively permitted/denied. UI actions: 'Activate Policy', 'Save as Active'. Enum: MONITOR_AND_ENFORCE.

cli_recipes.intent: Count policies currently in Active (monitor-and-enforce) mode for the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Single GraphQL call — returns {dateTime, monitorMode, value}.

cli_recipes.intent: List traffic that hit Active policies over the last 24h
cli_recipes.notes: PolicyStatus=ACTIVE corresponds to MONITOR_AND_ENFORCE.

cli_recipes.intent: Filter the full policy stream to only Active policies
cli_recipes.notes: JMESPath filter against the per-policy monitorMode field on get-all-policies-as-nd-json.

cli_recipes.intent: Activate a simulation policy (transition to enforce)
cli_recipes.notes: Use change-status to flip enforcement state. Run --help first to see required body shape; do NOT bulk-activate without an approved change window.

context: Collection of devices receiving the same security treatment. Can be Dynamic or Static, Global or Local.

cli_recipes.intent: List all policy groups (one JSON object per line)
cli_recipes.notes: Both --filters and --pageable are required by the endpoint; '{}' filter returns all PGs.

cli_recipes.intent: Get a single policy group by id with full detail
cli_recipes.notes: Pass the UUID returned by get-policy-groups-json.

cli_recipes.intent: List devices currently in a policy group
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the device roster for a single PG.

cli_recipes.intent: Count policy groups (local vs global) at the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Drop --local to get the combined count.

context: Reusable L4 traffic filtering template defining protocol, ports, and permit/deny actions.

cli_recipes.intent: List all security profiles (one JSON object per line)
cli_recipes.notes: Streaming ndjson — combine with -q to project a subset of fields.

cli_recipes.intent: Read a single security profile
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the L4 rule template for one profile.

cli_recipes.intent: Find every policy referencing a given security profile
cli_recipes.notes: Useful before editing or deleting a profile — surfaces blast radius.

context: Visual PG-to-PG grid. Colors: Allow (green), Deny (red), Custom (blue), No Policy (gray).

cli_recipes.intent: Discover policy set IDs (the matrix is per-policy-set)
cli_recipes.notes: Lists policy sets so you can pick an ID for get-matrix.

cli_recipes.intent: Get the full policy matrix (PG-to-PG grid as JSON) for a policy set
cli_recipes.notes: Use the id from recipe [0].

context: 0-100 metric for policy coverage quality. Also referred to as Policy Deployment Score. Simulation policies contribute only 10% weight.

cli_recipes.intent: Get the tenant-wide Zero Trust / Policy Enforcement Score headline number
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the single FloatMetricValue the CCC dashboard tile shows. Default snapshot is the previous full hour UTC.

cli_recipes.intent: Get the Policy Enforcement Score for a single policy set
cli_recipes.notes: Use `elisity policy get-all-as-nd-json -q '[].{id: id, name: name}'` to list policy set ids.

cli_recipes.intent: Per-policy-group device + policy coverage breakdown
cli_recipes.notes: Returns zeroTrustScore + leastPrivilegeScore per (site, PG, snapshot). The matrix behind the headline score.

cli_recipes.intent: Show the weights used to compute the Policy Enforcement Score
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the weights config (Simulation policies contribute ~10%).

context: IEC 62443 aligned criticality. SL1=Low Impact, SL2=Medium, SL3=High, SL4=Critical.

cli_recipes.intent: Discover which device attribute carries Security Level (per-tenant naming may vary)
cli_recipes.notes: Lists every device-attribute layer. Look for an attribute named like 'security_level' or 'iec_62443' — Security Level is modeled as a device attribute, not a top-level field.

cli_recipes.intent: List the values currently in use for a given attribute (e.g. SL1..SL4)
cli_recipes.notes: Confirms the enum values present in the IdentityGraph before building filter logic.

context: Logical grouping of Virtual Edge Nodes. Software-defined, not a physical appliance.

cli_recipes.intent: List all Virtual Edges (search/filter, no args = all)
cli_recipes.notes: Returns a paginated content[] list of VEs with id, name, veType, veVendor.

cli_recipes.intent: Count Virtual Edges for the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Single value per snapshot — the headline VE count.

cli_recipes.intent: Export every Virtual Edge to JSON
cli_recipes.notes: Bulk export — useful for inventory or backup before edits.

context: Existing switch onboarded as an Elisity enforcement point. No new hardware required.

cli_recipes.intent: List every Virtual Edge Node
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the full VEN inventory with status, model, and parent VE.

cli_recipes.intent: Get a single VEN by id
cli_recipes.notes: One VEN with full detail (interfaces, registration, firmware).

cli_recipes.intent: Count VENs by model for the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Per-model + per-type breakdown. Use --model to filter.

cli_recipes.intent: Export every VEN to JSON
cli_recipes.notes: Bulk export — useful for inventory or backup before edits.

context: A VEN deployment mode that monitors and reports network traffic without enforcing any policies. Used for pre-deployment network discovery, baselining traffic, and compliance auditing before activating policy enforcement.

cli_recipes.intent: List all VENs and inspect their mode field to find visibility-only ones
cli_recipes.notes: Visibility-only is a VEN deployment mode — inspect each VEN's mode/role attribute. Per-tenant attribute names vary; use `-q` to project once you know the field name.

cli_recipes.intent: Get a single VEN with full detail (mode, interfaces, registration)
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the VEN's deployment mode. Visibility-Only VENs do not push enforcement rules.

cli_recipes.intent: Inspect traffic from a Visibility-Only VEN's site (no enforcement, just visibility)
cli_recipes.notes: Useful for verifying pre-deployment baselining is collecting data before activating enforcement.

context: Elisity logical enforcement boundary. Can span multiple VLANs.

cli_recipes.intent: List every Distribution Zone
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the full DZ inventory with associated sites and VLAN ranges.

cli_recipes.intent: Get a single Distribution Zone by id
cli_recipes.notes: One DZ with VLAN membership and policy bindings.

cli_recipes.intent: Export every Distribution Zone
cli_recipes.notes: Bulk JSON export of all DZs.

cli_recipes.intent: List online devices grouped by Distribution Zone
cli_recipes.notes: Snapshot of how many live devices sit inside each DZ.

note: CCC is the platform the CLI talks to — there is no single CLI command that represents 'CCC'. To verify CLI connectivity to a specific CCC tenant use `elisity auth test`; to inspect the active connection use `elisity config show`.

context: Dynamic multi-source identity engine that constructs a holistic view of every network entity.

cli_recipes.intent: Get the device-attribute layer specifications backing the IdentityGraph
cli_recipes.notes: Enumerates every attribute layer (DHCP, AD, connector-sourced, etc.) the IdentityGraph composes.

cli_recipes.intent: Get a paginated devices view (IdentityGraph contents)
cli_recipes.notes: Body pagination is required — see Common pitfalls in docs/user-guide.md.

cli_recipes.intent: Get device counts broken out by source connector
cli_recipes.notes: Answers 'which connector contributes the most devices to the IdentityGraph?'

cli_recipes.intent: Tenant-wide online/offline device count
cli_recipes.notes: Single GraphQL call — much cheaper than paginating get-devices-view.

context: Accept/reject workflow for Insights classification recommendations. Statuses: PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED.

cli_recipes.intent: List policy suggestions awaiting adjudication
cli_recipes.notes: Returns suggestions whose status is one of PENDING/ACCEPTED/REJECTED.

cli_recipes.intent: List policy group classification suggestions
cli_recipes.notes: PG-classification suggestions — the most common adjudication surface.

cli_recipes.intent: Accept or reject (update) a suggestion
cli_recipes.notes: Run --help to see the required body shape; status field flips PENDING → ACCEPTED or REJECTED.

context: ML/LLM engine for device classification, policy group suggestions, and policy activation recommendations.

cli_recipes.intent: List all policy suggestions
cli_recipes.notes: Param-free GET; returns active suggestions across all categories.

cli_recipes.intent: List policy-activation suggestions
cli_recipes.notes: Policies Insights recommends activating (transition Simulation → Active).

cli_recipes.intent: Re-run the policy-suggestion pipeline
cli_recipes.notes: Forces Insights to recompute. Use sparingly — it kicks off a heavy job.

cli_recipes.intent: Inspect Insights engine settings
cli_recipes.notes: Returns thresholds and toggles controlling the ML/LLM engine.

context: System Policy Group where devices land when they don't match any Dynamic or Static Policy Group.

cli_recipes.intent: Find the Unassigned policy group in the PG list
cli_recipes.notes: Returns the PG entry whose name is exactly 'Unassigned'.

cli_recipes.intent: List every device currently in the Unassigned PG
cli_recipes.notes: Use the id from the previous command. Surfaces devices needing classification.

context: CCC feature for analyzing network traffic flows, top talkers, and policy action breakdowns.

cli_recipes.intent: Top N policy groups by traffic volume
cli_recipes.notes: Param-free aggregation across all traffic. Use --kind DENIED for blocked-only.

cli_recipes.intent: Get the latest raw traffic record set
cli_recipes.notes: Most recent flow batch — pair with -q to project src/dst/action.

cli_recipes.intent: Top N policy groups by traffic volume
cli_recipes.notes: MITRE-style top-talker view by PG.

cli_recipes.intent: Top N IPs by denied traffic
cli_recipes.notes: Top blocked IPs over the last 24h window.

context: Policy mode where enforcement is handled by an external system. Enum: MONITOR_EXTERNAL.

cli_recipes.intent: Count policies in Independent Control (external) mode at the latest snapshot
cli_recipes.notes: Returns {dateTime, monitorMode, value}.

cli_recipes.intent: Filter the full policy stream to only Independent Control policies
cli_recipes.notes: JMESPath filter on the per-policy monitorMode field on get-all-policies-as-nd-json.

context: The AI-powered chat feature in CCC for network security operations assistance.
note: Elisity Assistant is a CCC web-app feature — there is no direct CLI surface. Agents using the CLI play a similar role: see docs/AGENTS.md.
